questions.prompt: What does the operator's certificate cover?
options: Use of a mobile phone at sea
questions.explanation: The operator's certificate is personal. The installation is covered by a separate ship radio licence.

questions.prompt: Which factor most affects VHF range?
questions.explanation: VHF travels in nearly straight lines, so antenna height matters far more than power.

questions.prompt: Two antennas are each 4 m high. What is the approximate range?
What is the maximum transmit power of a fixed marine VHF radio?
questions.explanation: Fixed sets transmit up to 25 W, with a 1 W low-power setting for short-range use.

questions.prompt: What does the squelch control do?
options: Cuts background noise when no signal is present
questions.explanation: Set squelch so the hiss just disappears; too high and weak signals are lost.

questions.prompt: What does 'secrecy of correspondence' mean?
options: You must not disclose or use traffic not intended for you
You must not talk about your own position
Calls may only be made in English
questions.explanation: You may hear other people's calls, but you must not repeat or use them. Distress, urgency and safety traffic are the exception.

questions.prompt: Why is VHF better than a mobile phone in an emergency?
options: Every station in range hears the call
It works anywhere in the world
questions.explanation: A VHF call reaches rescuers and nearby vessels at once. A phone reaches one person.

questions.prompt: What does dual watch do?
options: Transmits on two channels at once
Monitors Channel 16 and one other channel in turn
questions.explanation: Dual watch alternates between Channel 16 and a selected channel so you do not miss calls on 16.

questions.prompt: What is Channel 16 used for?
questions.explanation: Make contact on 16, then move to a working channel.

questions.prompt: Which channel is used only for DSC?
questions.explanation: Channel 70 carries DSC data only. Voice is never used on it.

questions.prompt: What is Channel 13 mainly used for?
questions.explanation: Channel 13 is for bridge-to-bridge navigation safety.

questions.prompt: Which is the primary intership safety channel?
questions.explanation: Channel 6 is for intership safety and search and rescue coordination, not routine chat.

questions.prompt: How should you end a transmission when you expect a reply?
questions.explanation: OVER invites a reply. OUT ends the exchange. Never combine them.

questions.prompt: No reply to your routine call on Channel 16. How long should you wait before calling again?
questions.explanation: Waiting keeps Channel 16 clear and gives the other station time to respond.

questions.prompt: Where should a radio check be made?
options: On a working channel, or by DSC test call where supported
questions.explanation: Keep Channel 16 clear. Use a working channel or a DSC test call.

questions.prompt: You heard a call for your vessel but not who was calling. What do you say?
questions.explanation: STATION CALLING is the correct proword when the caller's name was not heard.

questions.prompt: How many digits does an MMSI have?
questions.explanation: An MMSI is always nine digits.

questions.prompt: What do the first three digits of a ship's MMSI show?
questions.explanation: The MID identifies the country. UK ships use 232 to 235.

questions.prompt: A coast station MMSI begins with…
questions.explanation: Coast stations start with 00. Group MMSIs start with a single 0.

questions.prompt: How do you send a DSC distress alert?
options: Lift the cover and hold the distress button for about 5 seconds
questions.explanation: Hold the red button for about five seconds. Choose the nature of distress first if time allows.

questions.prompt: What happens after a DSC distress alert is sent?
options: The radio switches to Channel 16 and repeats the alert until acknowledged
The radio waits on Channel 70 for a voice reply
questions.explanation: Wait briefly for acknowledgement, then send your voice Mayday on 16.

questions.prompt: In coastal waters, how should another yacht respond to a DSC distress alert it receives?
options: Listen on Channel 16 and leave acknowledgement to the coast station
questions.explanation: Coast stations acknowledge. Listen on 16 and be ready to help or relay.

questions.prompt: You sent a DSC distress alert by mistake. What should you do?
options: Switch the radio off and say nothing
Cancel on the radio if possible and make a voice cancellation on Channel 16
questions.explanation: Do not switch off. Cancel and announce the cancellation by voice on 16 straight away.

questions.prompt: Why should a DSC radio be connected to GPS?
options: So the distress alert includes your position
It is needed to change channels
questions.explanation: Without a position feed, rescuers receive your identity but not where you are.

questions.prompt: When is a Mayday appropriate?
options: Engine failure in open water, no danger
Grave and imminent danger needing immediate assistance
questions.explanation: Mayday is for grave and imminent danger only.

questions.prompt: Which signal is used for an urgent message where danger is not yet grave and imminent?
questions.explanation: PAN-PAN is the urgency signal.

questions.prompt: A floating container is drifting in a busy channel. Which signal fits?
questions.explanation: SÉCURITÉ announces navigation and weather safety information.

questions.prompt: In the Mayday call, what follows the vessel's identification?
questions.explanation: Order: Mayday, identify, position, nature, assistance, number, information, over.

questions.prompt: What does SEELONCE MAYDAY mean?
options: Silence, imposed by the station controlling distress traffic
questions.explanation: Only the controlling station uses SEELONCE MAYDAY.

questions.prompt: Which proword means distress traffic has ended?
questions.explanation: SEELONCE FEENEE: normal working may resume.

questions.prompt: When would you send a MAYDAY RELAY?
options: When you are in distress yourself
When passing on a distress message the coastguard may not have received
To ask for a radio check
questions.explanation: A relay passes on another vessel's distress, for example when the casualty is out of the coastguard's range.

questions.prompt: How should a Sécurité message be handled on Channel 16?
options: Announce on 16 and give a working channel for the full message
Wait for permission from the coastguard
questions.explanation: Keep 16 clear by moving the full message to a working channel.

questions.prompt: What does PRUDONCE mean?
questions.explanation: PRUDONCE allows restricted working during distress traffic.

questions.prompt: Sea Area A1 is defined by coverage of…
questions.explanation: A1 is within range of a shore VHF DSC station, typically 20 to 30 nautical miles.

questions.prompt: On what frequency does an EPIRB send its satellite distress signal?
questions.explanation: 406 MHz goes to satellites. 121.5 MHz is for homing.

questions.prompt: Why must an EPIRB be registered?
options: So rescuers know whose beacon it is and who to contact
questions.explanation: Registration links the beacon to your vessel and emergency contacts.

questions.prompt: How does a radar SART appear on a rescuer's radar?
questions.explanation: A radar SART shows as 12 dots extending outwards from your position.

questions.prompt: What should you do if you activate a beacon by accident?
options: Switch it off and tell the coastguard straight away
Remove the battery and say nothing
questions.explanation: Switching off and informing the coastguard prevents a needless search.

questions.prompt: On what frequency is international NAVTEX broadcast in English?
questions.explanation: 518 kHz carries the international service in English. 490 kHz is often national language.

questions.prompt: How is a PLB different from an EPIRB?
options: It is registered to a person and activated by hand
questions.explanation: A PLB is personal and manually activated.

questions.prompt: How is the letter J spelled phonetically?
questions.explanation: The international spelling is JULIETT with two Ts.

questions.prompt: How should the number 9 be spoken?
questions.explanation: NIN-ER avoids confusion with the German 'nein'.

questions.prompt: Which proword means 'I have finished and expect a reply'?
questions.explanation: OVER invites a reply.

questions.prompt: Which proword asks the other station to repeat?
questions.explanation: SAY AGAIN means please repeat. I SAY AGAIN is used when you repeat.

questions.prompt: Which time standard is used in distress and safety messages?
questions.explanation: Use the 24-hour clock in UTC.

questions.prompt: What is 1 nautical mile in metres?
questions.explanation: 1 nautical mile = 1,852 metres.

questions.prompt: A position given as a bearing and distance uses a bearing…
options: Magnetic, from you to the point
True, from the charted point to you
questions.explanation: Bearings are given in degrees true, from the charted point to your position.
